sourceRef: docs/architecture/item/spec-salvage-craft.md (item module 14) - D7, D23, D24, D26, D29, and ssot-materials-crafting.md (I9) sections 5.1, 7.4. A balance pass owns this file, not code (tunables-ssot.md). Every quantity the cost path and the salvage path read is here; MaterialTuning.cs is a pure parser with no defaults.

grade.note: I9 5.1: grade = 1 + min(maxGrade-1, itemLevel / itemLevelPerGrade), integer division. STRUCTURAL on the maxGrade side - four substrate grades ship (crude/sound/fine/prime) and a fifth would be a new material id, not a balance edit. itemLevelPerGrade is a real tunable: it is where the grade lock's steepness lives.

upcycle.capNote: BOUNDED RATIO, exempt from AGENTS.md's no-hard-ceilings rule and required to say so. maxInputGrade caps a CONVERSION between two material grades (crude->sound->fine); it is not a ceiling on how much a player may earn, own, or spend. Without it, volume-farming level-10 content manufactures prime substrate and the grade lock (I9 5.3) stops meaning anything - which is the exact failure the cap exists to prevent, not a progression stop. inputPerOutput is the drain valve I9 7.3 names: 'if substrate inflates past usefulness anyway, the drain valve is the upcycle recipe ratio - a data edit, not a redesign.'

forgeGemRungNote: species-gear-chain T9 (spec-gem-tier.md OQ2): the forge-gem verb feeds the OUTPUT gem tier as the RecipeContext rung input. That rung index is a 0..9 ladder position while a gem tier is 1..5 - the scale mismatch is deliberate and stated here, not a bug: pricing the legs on the output tier is what makes a t4 upcycle cost more than a t2, and rung-variable legs (souls x30, essence x3) are the drain. Prose only - no number in this file moves for it.

costBandMultiplierPerMille.mirrorNote: MIRRORS data/seed/items/_registry/bands.v1.json costBand.multiplierTable, which is FROZEN at registryVersion 1 and is the authority. It is mirrored here rather than read from there because Core never reads a file (tunables-ssot.md 7.2) and the registry is a seed-authoring artefact, not a tuning file. MaterialCorpusTests asserts the two agree value-for-value against the real registry, so a drift is a red test rather than a silent 2x price change.
costBandMultiplierPerMille.applicationNote: bands.v1.json's own formula: resolvedQty = max(1, ceil(baseQty * multiplierPerMille / 1000)). Ceiling always, so no band can make a cost free.

upcycle.note: substrate is a FLAT 5, not 5 x g - I9 7.4 reads 'five of grade g -> one of grade g+1', a fixed conversion ratio. It is upcycle.inputPerOutput and the two are asserted equal at parse time.

imbue.note: D24 - the tenth row, which I9 7.4 has no line for at all. The souls and substrate legs are bore's VERBATIM (50/3, both rung-linear), per D24's ruling that imbuing prices on the same curve as boring; the one addition is the essence leg, because essence is the class whose whole job is direction without magnitude and imbue is the operation that names which element a hole becomes. Asserted equal to bore's legs by test, so a balance pass that moves bore and forgets imbue goes red.

socket.bandImmuneNote: I9 7.4 states this as a RULE, not an illustration: 'socketing an insert costs 10 souls and nothing else - moving a gem you already own between sockets must never be a material decision, or players stop experimenting and the socket system dies quietly.' A costBand multiplier on this leg would make the number the author's rather than the rule's - recipe.022 in the shipped corpus authors soulsCostBand 'cheap', which would resolve it to 5 and quietly contradict the rule. bandImmune keeps the rule; the band is still parsed and still validated, it just does not scale this leg.

reroll-all.note: spec-salvage-craft.md's re-issued table prints 'b flux' in the ESSENCE column and leaves Catalyst blank for this row - a column shift introduced when the row was re-typed. I9 7.4, the source, has essence '-' and catalyst 'b flux'. The source wins; recorded in tasks/item-todo.md P4.1 as a spec defect.

repair.note: species-gear-chain T23 first values. D5 shape, matching elevate: souls+substrate+catalyst.temper at low/mid rungs, +shard at top rungs. A balance pass owns these; T49 retunes.

upgrade.note: E5: the upgrade consumes the input chassis and climbs one rung, so it prices on the rung above elevate (60) and pays souls only - the consumed item IS the material cost. First value; a later balance pass (T49-style) owns it.

salvageCoefficient.derivationNote: I9 5.1's salvage_coefficient is FOUR rows keyed on the retired four-band ladder. Re-derived here to ten rungs the same way module 7 re-derived I12's drop weights and module 11 re-solved I12's pity thresholds: hold the source's own anchors exactly, and interpolate by a stated rule rather than by feel. The four anchors are not chosen - they are LegacyCreatureRarityIds.ForwardMap, the shipped one-way band->rung map (common->chaff 0, rare->cultivated 3, epic->heirloom 6, legendary->sunwoven 8), so common's row lands on chaff, rare's on cultivated, epic's on heirloom and legendary's on sunwoven, value for value. Between anchors: integer linear interpolation with FLOOR, never round-half-up, because rounding a salvage yield UP is the only direction that can break R2's strict-loss invariant. Above the top anchor (almanac, rung 9): substrateBase and shardBack continue the last segment's slope, floored; essenceCap stays flat, because I9's own table already stopped it growing at epic (3 at both epic and legendary) - the flat tail is the source's shape, not an invention. MaterialCorpusTests re-computes all thirty numbers from the four anchors plus this rule and asserts the file matches, so an edit by feel goes red with the derivation named.

salvageEnhanceReturnNote: I9 5.1: catalyst.temper x (enh / divisor), integer division. Strictly lossy against temper's own catalyst leg (ceil((n+1)/3) spent per level, floor(n/3) returned in total), which is one of R2's three locks. There is deliberately NO upper bound on the return - a long enhancement history returns proportionally more temper, and that is the converter working, not a leak.

speciesCostMultiplierMilli.note: species-gear-chain T32: one multiplier per rung, MH-shaped -- flat (neutral 1000) below the gate, escalating 1500/2000/3000/4000 from heirloom up. Chosen to sit inside the existing costBandMultiplierPerMille order of magnitude (500..8000) so a gated species piece costs comparably to a steep-to-exorbitant band recipe, never a new scale.
